title: Jatayu
hook: a prince gives a dying bird the rites of a son

segments.voice: Yesterday: the old vulture broke Ravana's bow and chariot, and lost his wings. Wings given for a promise.

Rama comes back from killing the deer, meets Lakshmana on the path, and knows before he gets there. The hut is empty. Valmiki lets Rama come apart. He runs from tree to tree asking where she went. He asks the river. He asks the deer, and the deer turn and look south. His grief turns to rage, and he says he'll tear the worlds apart, until Lakshmana talks him down. Then, on the ground ahead, they see something huge, and bleeding.
screen: `THE EMPTY HUT.` → `THE DEER LOOK SOUTH.` → `SOMETHING ON THE GROUND.`

segments.voice: At first Rama thinks it's a demon that has eaten Sita, and he draws his bow. Then the bird speaks. It's Jatayu, and he's dying. With what breath he has left, he tells them: Ravana took her. I fought him. He cut me down and flew south. He tries to say more. Valmiki has him begin: Ravana, son of Vishravas, brother of Kubera, the lord of wealth. Then the words stop, and he dies. He spends his last breath the way Sita spent her voice, on the message. Holding the body, Rama tells Lakshmana that this bird lived long in the forest and has died for them, and deserves the same honor as their own father. Remember, Rama wasn't there when Dasharatha's body was burned; he heard the news in the forest, from Bharata. Now Rama builds a pyre himself and performs the last rites for a vulture, as a son would. He offers the water and speaks the verses, and Valmiki says Jatayu goes to the highest worlds. A vulture king's death gets a prince's rites. And the first thing Rama does after learning who took Sita isn't revenge. It's a funeral. Before he hunts the one who took her, he honors the one who tried to save her.
screen: `A DEMON? NO: JATAYU, DYING.` · `HIS LAST BREATH: THE MESSAGE.` · `A SON'S RITES FOR A BIRD.` · `A FUNERAL BEFORE REVENGE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who helped you and is gone, or far away, or simply never thanked, and let their face come up. Breathe in and remember one thing they did; breathe out and let the thanks be there, unspoken. If nobody comes to mind, think of a stranger who once did you a small kindness.
Jatayu. His last breath goes to the message, and Rama burns him on a pyre with a son's rites.
Your line: a funeral before revenge. Tomorrow, the forest gets stranger still. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindu funeral rites (antyeshti) are usually performed by a son or close relative; some teachers tell Rama's rites for Jatayu as a sign that loyalty can make someone family.

fork.setup: you're Rama. the vulture who fought for Sita has just died in front of you. what do you do?
options: leave at once to chase Ravana.
build a pyre and perform the last rites yourself.
ask Lakshmana to bury him while you go on.
fork.reveal: Rama performs Jatayu's funeral himself, as a son for a father, before anything else.

original.note: Sanskrit gṛdhrarāja: king of vultures, a title Valmiki gives Jatayu.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama mourns a helpful bird.
what it means: he gives Jatayu the full rites a son gives a father.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 68 has Jatayu name Ravana as son of Vishravas and brother of Kubera before dying; Rama's cremation of him follows in the same sarga.

chat.says: Rama just learned Ravana took Sita. Why stop to hold a funeral for a bird?
options: Jatayu died trying to save Sita, so Rama honored him the way a son honors a father.
Rama needed the funeral fire as a signal to call allies from across the forest.
Jatayu asked to be burned in exchange for telling Rama where Ravana lived.
chat.meaning: Rama said Jatayu deserved the same honor as their own father, and gave him a son's rites before hunting Ravana: a funeral before revenge.

Jatayu.meaning: the old vulture king who fought Ravana for Sita

Vishravas.meaning: Ravana's father, named in Jatayu's last words

Kubera.meaning: the lord of wealth, Ravana's brother

Dasharatha.meaning: Rama's father, who died while Rama was in exile

Bharata.meaning: Rama's brother, who brought news of their father's death

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 60–66 (Rama's search and grief; Lakshmana calms him)
Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 67–68 (Jatayu's last words and funeral)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering and differ between editions; confirm against the edition the Keeper uses.
The deer looking/running south and Rama's threat to destroy the worlds: confirm sargas (around Aranya 64).
Jatayu's final words (son of Vishravas, brother of Kubera): paraphrased; confirm.
'Rama wasn't there when Dasharatha's body was burned': Rama hears of his father's death at Chitrakuta from Bharata (Ayodhya Kanda) and offers water then; confirm framing.
